packet.description_seed: Israel's PM laughed off reports of friction, but he has tested the patience of other US presidents.

what: 'Crazy' phone call between Trump and Netanyahu complicates Iran talks

clean_source_blocks.text: Israel's PM laughed off reports of friction, but he has tested the patience of other US presidents.

Trump added: "I like Bibi a lot. And I work very well with him." He would be far from the only US president to tangle with the Israeli PM. The prime minister has a long history of testing the White House's patience - and of politically surviving any fallout. The latest reported clash came as Trump mulls a deal that would extend the US-Iran ceasefire and open the door to talks on the future of Tehran's nuclear programme. The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz - a vital global shipping lane - is also at stake. Netanyahu laughed off any suggestion of tensions with his American ally.

Donald Trump has become the latest US president to find himself at odds with Benjamin Netanyahu, after reportedly clashing with the Israeli prime minister over military action in Lebanon that has thrown Washington's Iran diplomacy into crisis. Tehran responded to Israel's strikes on Lebanon by threatening to suspend talks with the US - a potential setback to Trump's efforts to extricate himself from an unpopular war with Iran. Trump was asked by a journalist about an Axios report that he had called Netanyahu "effing crazy" and accused him of ingratitude during a phone call on Monday. "I did," Trump told the Pod Force One podcast in an interview broadcast on Wednesday. "I wouldn't say angry. I was a little bit perturbed at his constantly fighting with ​Lebanon, you know."

"Sometimes we have, as in the best of families, you have these tactical disagreements," he told CNBC in an interview on Wednesday. "We always find a way to work them out, and we do so as great friends." He added that the two can "disagree in the morning" and be in agreement by afternoon. Experts, however, cautioned that the call could point to frustration in the White House over the alignment of US and Israeli military and political goals nearly 100 days after they launched strikes on targets in Iran on 28 February. "Netanyahu has a long history of doing his own dance, irrespective of what he has heard from Washington," Brett Bruen, a former diplomat and president of crisis communications agency the Global Situation Room, told the BBC.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Donald Trump has become the latest US president to find himself at odds with Benjamin Netanyahu, after reportedly clashing with the Israeli prime minister over military action in Lebanon that has thrown Washington's Iran diplomacy into crisis.

Tehran responded to Israel's strikes on Lebanon by threatening to suspend talks with the US - a potential setback to Trump's efforts to extricate himself from an unpopular war with Iran.

Trump was asked by a journalist about an Axios report that he had called Netanyahu "effing crazy" and accused him of ingratitude during a phone call on Monday.

"I did," Trump told the Pod Force One podcast in an interview broadcast on Wednesday. "I wouldn't say angry. I was a little bit perturbed at his constantly fighting with ​Lebanon, you know."

Trump added: "I like Bibi a lot. And I work very well with him."

He would be far from the only US president to tangle with the Israeli PM. The prime minister has a long history of testing the White House's patience - and of politically surviving any fallout.

The latest reported clash came as Trump mulls a deal that would extend the US-Iran ceasefire and open the door to talks on the future of Tehran's nuclear programme.

The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz - a vital global shipping lane - is also at stake.

Netanyahu laughed off any suggestion of tensions with his American ally.

"Sometimes we have, as in the best of families, you have these tactical disagreements," he told CNBC in an interview on Wednesday. "We always find a way to work them out, and we do so as great friends."

He added that the two can "disagree in the morning" and be in agreement by afternoon.

Experts, however, cautioned that the call could point to frustration in the White House over the alignment of US and Israeli military and political goals nearly 100 days after they launched strikes on targets in Iran on 28 February.

"Netanyahu has a long history of doing his own dance, irrespective of what he has heard from Washington," Brett Bruen, a former diplomat and president of crisis communications agency the Global Situation Room, told the BBC.

"Trump… decided to take the plunge with him, and is now learning a really hard lesson about what happens when you get into war with a pretty mercurial leader that has an agenda which doesn't always align with your own priorities," he added.

Broadly, Netanyahu and Trump agree on the key US objective of preventing Iran from manufacturing or having a nuclear weapon.

payload.title: Trumpin ja Netanjahun puhelu kiristää Iran-neuvottelujen asetelmaa
payload.summary: Donald Trumpin ja Benjamin Netanjahun välinen raportoitu kiista on vaikeuttanut Washingtonin Iran-diplomatiaa tilanteessa, jossa Yhdysvallat pyrkii jatkamaan tulitaukoa ja avaamaan keskusteluja Teheranin ydinohjelmasta.
payload.content:
Donald Trumpin ja Israelin pääministerin Benjamin Netanjahun välille raportoitu puhelinkiista on noussut uudeksi jännitteeksi Yhdysvaltojen Iran-diplomatiassa. Taustalla on Israelin sotilaallinen toiminta Libanonissa, johon Teheran on reagoinut uhkaamalla keskeyttää neuvottelut Washingtonin kanssa.

## Kiista osuu herkkään neuvotteluhetkeen

Trump on pohtimassa sopimusta, joka pidentäisi Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin välistä tulitaukoa ja voisi avata tien keskusteluille Teheranin ydinohjelman tulevaisuudesta. Samalla vaakalaudalla on Hormuzinsalmen uudelleen avaaminen. Salmi on keskeinen maailmanlaajuiselle meriliikenteelle.

Raportoidun kiistan mukaan Trump olisi moittinut Netanjahua maanantaisessa puhelussa ja syyttänyt tätä kiittämättömyydestä. Kun Trumpilta kysyttiin Axiosin raportista, jonka mukaan hän olisi kutsunut Netanjahua karkeasti hulluksi, hän vahvisti Pod Force One -podcastissa asian, mutta vähätteli suuttumustaan. Trumpin mukaan hän oli pikemminkin hieman ärtynyt siitä, että Netanjahu jatkaa jatkuvaa taistelua Libanonin kanssa.

Trump korosti silti suhteen toimivuutta. Hän sanoi pitävänsä Netanjahusta paljon ja työskentelevänsä tämän kanssa hyvin.

## Netanjahu vähättelee välirikkoa

Netanjahu on torjunut kuvan vakavasta välirikosta. Hän kuvasi CNBC:n haastattelussa erimielisyyksiä taktisiksi ja vertasi niitä parhaiden perheiden sisäisiin kiistoihin. Hänen mukaansa osapuolet löytävät aina tavan ratkaista asiat ystävinä. Netanjahu lisäsi, että kaksikko voi olla aamulla eri mieltä ja iltapäivällä jälleen samalla kannalla.

Asiantuntijat ovat kuitenkin varoittaneet, että puhelu voi kertoa Valkoisen talon turhautumisesta siihen, miten Yhdysvaltojen ja Israelin sotilaalliset ja poliittiset tavoitteet sopivat yhteen. Jännite nousee esiin lähes sata päivää sen jälkeen, kun maat aloittivat iskut Iranissa oleviin kohteisiin 28. helmikuuta.

Entinen diplomaatti Brett Bruen arvioi, että Netanjahulla on pitkä historia oman linjansa ajamisesta riippumatta siitä, mitä Washingtonista on kuultu. Trump ei olisi ensimmäinen Yhdysvaltain presidentti, jonka kärsivällisyyttä Israelin pääministeri on koetellut. Netanjahu on myös aiemmin selvinnyt poliittisesti tällaisista törmäyksistä.
summary_bullets: Trumpin ja Netanjahun raportoitu puhelinkiista on vaikeuttanut Yhdysvaltojen Iran-diplomatiaa.
Teheran on uhannut keskeyttää neuvottelut Yhdysvaltojen kanssa Israelin Libanonin-iskujen jälkeen.
Netanjahu vähätteli jännitteitä ja kuvasi niitä taktisiksi erimielisyyksiksi ystävien välillä.
